title: The environment tier: a sandbox pool that scales on its queue
purpose: Give every answer four tool calls in a sandbox pool and compare a fixed pool of two workers with a pool that KEDA scales on the length of its queue. Measure what the rollout fleet and the trainer see.

steps.display: kubectl -n rl-scale get lws rollout   # 2 engine(s), settings: defaults
kubectl apply -f sandbox-pool.yaml   # fixed pool, 2 workers; every call takes 250 ms of 'tool time' plus the code's run
kubectl apply -f trainer-env-fixed.yaml   # a JobSet: fixed pool, 2 workers
steps.output:
CKPT_EVERY=1000
EVAL_EVERY=0
EVAL_PROBLEMS=200
GPUS_HELD=3
LEARNING_RATE=3e-6
MAX_COMPLETION=512
MAX_CONCURRENT=64
MAX_STEPS=5
TASK=pyexec
TOOL_CALLS=4
WATCHDOG_S=900

steps.display: kubectl apply -f sandbox-pool.yaml   # pool scaled by queue length, 2 to 40 workers; every call takes 250 ms of 'tool time' plus the code's run
kubectl apply -f trainer-env-keda.yaml   # a JobSet: pool scaled by queue length, 2 to 40 workers
steps.output:
CKPT_EVERY=1000
EVAL_EVERY=0
EVAL_PROBLEMS=200
GPUS_HELD=3
LEARNING_RATE=3e-6
MAX_COMPLETION=512

steps.display: python compare.py env-fixed env-keda   # 5 steps each, four tool calls per answer
steps.output:

peak sandbox workers                                  2            12
peak queue length (calls waiting)                    30            28
calls served                                       8576          8032
median seconds per step                           191.3          41.5
time to score a group (median s)                    4.5           1.0
trainer waiting for samples (median s)            188.3          37.7
tokens generated per second                          87           372

steps.display: kubectl get deploy sandbox-workers   # a few minutes after the run, with the queue empty

checks.description: with two workers the queue builds up and the trainer's step is dominated by waiting for rewards
checks.because: Two workers serve about eight calls a second. A group of eight answers with four calls each is thirty-two calls, and the trainer needs about twenty groups for one step.

checks.description: KEDA grows the pool when the queue grows: at least four times the starting size
checks.because: KEDA reads the length of the Redis list every five seconds and sets the replica count to the length divided by the target per worker (two), up to the maximum. The trainer scores one group at a time, so at most about thirty messages wait, which caps the pool near fifteen. Scaling on CPU would react only after the workers were busy.

checks.description: the scaled pool at least halves the step
checks.because: Same recipe, same model, same hardware. Only the number of workers behind the queue differs.

checks.description: the pool shrinks back when the queue is empty
checks.because: The cooldown is sixty seconds. A pool that stays large costs CPU for nothing; one that never grew costs GPU time, as the fixed pool showed.

checks.description: the queue is drained at the end: no call was lost
checks.because: Every call is a message that a worker removes with a blocking pop and answers on its own result list, so a message is either waiting, being served, or answered.
